points.text: CircuitLens still needs an explainer LLM and large dataset, contradicting the stated motivation.
Figure 1 is uninformative; should illustrate each step with subfigures.
Section 3.2 is poorly contextualized relative to previous subsection and goal.
Section 3.2 workflow hard to follow; explanations should be reordered.
Evaluation covers only four layers.
Evaluation criteria could be aggregated into a single score for comparison.
Motivation and exposition unclear for Assumption 2 and circuit-based clustering.
Faithfulness scores very low; doubtful descriptions reflect feature behavior.
Unclear how methods in Sections 3.1-3.2 map to methods evaluated in Section 4.
Unclear which techniques are new; output-effect analysis is standard logit lens.
Need qualitative examples of annotator inputs and resulting labels per method.
Writing needs editing: long sentences, takeaway format, no clear narrative.
Puri et al. metrics described too briefly.
No validation of LLM-as-judge metrics, e.g., against human annotations.
Baselines Neuronpedia and MaxAct* insufficiently described.
Unclear whether method works on other sparse dictionaries like SAEs.
Cost of circuit-based analyses not given; methods may be too expensive and niche.
No implementation available for non-trivial method.
Robustness claim in abstract is untested.
Efficiency claim has no cost numbers.
Conclusion's 58.8% coverage refers to GPT-2 while tests use Gemma.
Evaluation limited to four layers of one model.
No repeated runs or intervals to judge differences.
No human check of descriptions.
Choice of layers and feature sampling not stated.
Results sections mix model facts and findings; no limitations section.
Typos in Table 1 and text.
No human evaluation of whether descriptions are understandable; FADE is LLM-only.
Lemmatization blurs morphological features; no linguistic analysis of validation failures.
Applicability to multilingual, code or multimodal settings unaddressed.
Safety motivation asserted but no downstream use demonstrated.
Selection of qualitative examples in Figures 5-6 not described.
Evaluated feature population undefined; may condition on WeightLens success.
Same baselines have different scores in Tables 1 and 2.
No variance, intervals or tests; many differences tiny.
Circuit contribution confounded with prompt, sampling, masking; no ablation.
Table 2 shows trade-off: Clarity up, Purity down, not uniform gain.
Efficiency and scalability claimed but cost never measured.
Key parameters (z-threshold, rho, DBSCAN, judge model) missing.
No hyperparameter sensitivity analysis.
Validation forward-pass context unspecified; cannot test context-independence of Assumption 2.
Abstract 'matching or exceeding' contradicted by Purity and Faithfulness.
'Perform poorly' statement about layers inconsistent with Table 1.
Table 1 cell '0.7' likely a typo.
Output component lowers Clarity; 'LLM postprocessing not essential' undiscussed.
Weight-space method not positioned against prior vocabulary-projection work; novelty delta unstated.
No plain unembedding-projection baseline.
No comparison with embedding-based clustering (Kopf et al.); insufficiency claim untested.
Baselines narrow; cited auto-interp methods not run.
Assumptions are heuristics; Assumption 2 contradicted by context-dependence finding.
Raw transcoder weights used despite interference problem paper describes.
RoPE explanation stated as finding rather than hypothesis.
Inconsistent method naming and typo 'WeigthLens'.
Clarity metric sensitive to format; evidence supports only LLM-judged Clarity.
Abstract claim of matching or exceeding contradicted by Purity, Faithfulness.
Possible selection bias: evaluated features may condition on method success.
Tables 1 and 2 give different baseline values.
CircuitLens changes several factors together; no ablation isolates circuits.
Claim of removing dataset and LLM dependence contradicted for CircuitLens.
Cost never measured despite scalability claims.
Causal explanations (l0, RoPE) asserted without test.
Table 1 caption error, '0.7' cell, typo.
Clustering and threshold parameters not given.
Qualitative cases lack stated selection rule.
Eq. 4 lacks Jacobian for earlier heads, unlike Eq. 2.

P.summary: CircuitLens still depends on explainer LLM and dataset.
Method names not linked between method and evaluation sections.
LLM-judge metrics not validated against humans.
Cost not reported; possibly too expensive.

Q.summary: Efficiency and scalability claimed but cost unmeasured.
Coverage number attributed to wrong model.
Evaluation limited to four layers of one model.
No human validation; LLM-judged metrics of limited validity.
Evaluated feature population undefined; selection bias.
Results presentation mixes facts and findings; no limitations.
Lemmatization and linguistic analysis of failures.
Table 2 shows trade-off, not uniform gain.
Assumption 2 heuristic and validation step cannot test it.
Not positioned against prior weight/vocabulary-space analysis.
